findings.current: Existing WebDAV uses a single account-local outbox, scope, epoch, pending and cursor map. ACK deletes rows through the persisted through marker in the same transaction as clearing pending and advancing cursor. No LAN ACK path or independent target delivery state found.
findings.risk: Reusing current global deletion for a second target can remove the only local replay payload while another target is pending. No observed live two-target data loss is claimed.
findings.required: Persist authenticated per-target obligations and receipts plus immutable replay bytes and a stable cross-channel batch identity. Gate all ACK/rebind/GC paths, include both ACK orders, repeated and stale ACK, restart and WAN-isolated replay, missing or damaged payload, setting changes and target revocation.

findings.current: SQLite pending commit precedes immutable conditional PUT, matching body is required on path collision, manifest uses strong ETag CAS, and ACK follows cloud publication. Received events and contiguous cursor commit together. Snapshot parts commit separately and cursor is advanced after all parts validate.
limits: no proof against unauthorized server modification
no arbitrary physical power loss or fsync evidence
historical malformed or nonmatching recovery state must fail closed

findings.current: Windows renews and checks the current lease token before sending a request. Post-I/O native ACK, pull apply and manifest cache mutations have no equivalent token check in their mutation transaction.
findings.risk: Delayed response across expiry and competing acquisition may let old session mutate pending or cursor under newer session. Evidence does not establish data loss or reproduction.
findings.required: Cloud-only interleaving with delayed response, takeover, new pending and scope/epoch transition. Validate token and matching context in native mutation transaction or demonstrate equivalent fence. For isolated D1 work keep all sync and competing access outside migration windows.

findings.current: C and shared JS use deterministic field ordering, actor/seq and causality. Android executes the shared JS logic against Java SQLite. Retained contradictory fields at the same event identity are rejected. Existing v2 shape remains compatible with valid legacy batches.
limits: no unbounded or independent multi-target replay/dedup ledger
new kinds must await explicit compatibility gate
no arbitrary historical binary or live mixed-version fleet claim

findings.current: Shared JS migration preserves immutable v1 backup, commit marker, tombstones and initial retained snapshot before manifest publication. Windows rejects an unfinished legacy backup migration; a supported JS/Android migrator must finish first. Fresh-actor snapshot restore and same-original-database lease-expiry recovery have distinct scoped evidence.
